verdicts.reason: A: the reading order is sound, but the CTA is shrunk to a tiny pill with barely legible text, buried bottom-left under a large dead band below the product. The headline nearly touches the right edge, and the body copy runs over the circle. B: the CTA is large and legible but sits at the top, ahead of the logo and headline, which breaks the reading order; the logo floats off-axis at right, the headline is jammed against the right edge and the bottom third is empty. B still keeps the CTA usable and the product→headline→copy flow coherent, so it is marginally less broken.
